headline: £2 a day to Amazon residents protects rainforest, study shows
meta_description: A pilot project paying people in the Amazon £2 daily has proven effective at protecting rainforest, offering a new conservation model.
summary_short: A pilot project paying Amazon residents £2 per day has successfully protected rainforest, demonstrating a practical conservation approach.
body:
A pilot project offering small daily payments to people living in the Amazon has proven effective at protecting the rainforest, research shows.

The initiative tested whether modest financial incentives could motivate communities to preserve forest rather than exploit it. By providing £2 daily to participants, the project created direct economic benefit tied to forest protection, shifting the balance away from logging or clearing land.

This approach addresses a core challenge in conservation: people living in or near threatened ecosystems often face immediate economic pressure to use natural resources. Rather than imposing restrictions from outside, the pilot worked with local communities by recognizing their needs. The results suggest that conservation doesn't require choosing between protecting nature and supporting livelihoods—it can do both.
quick_facts: Pilot project pays £2 per day to Amazon residents
Payment-for-protection model successfully reduces rainforest damage
Combines conservation with local economic support
